findings.how_to_check: In a fresh Stata session where PERSONAL and PLUS directories do not already contain ABE commands, run `do replication/config.do` followed by `which abeclean` and `which abematch`. Both will return error 111 ('command not found') despite copies existing under LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the repository ABE implementation to the ado-path in replication/config.do (e.g. `adopath ++ "$REP_REPO/LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/reference"`), or copy abeclean.ado, abematch.ado, and their dependencies into replication/stata/.
findings.title: The new FamilySearch linking pipeline depends on ABE commands that are not placed on Stata's ado-path
findings.what_the_code_does: MATCHING/1b_fs_divided_files.do:65 directly calls `abeclean` and MATCHING/2_ABE_matchingV3_christian_torben.do:158 calls `abematch`. However, replication/config.do:44 only adds `$REP_REPO/replication/stata` (which contains only repnum.ado) to the ado-path, and assigning `global MatchingDoFiles` in MATCHING/2_ABE_matchingV3_christian_torben.do:44 points to an external Dropbox folder without issuing an `adopath ++` command.
findings.why_it_matters: An external replicator running the master matching script or placebo check on a clean checkout will fail immediately with unrecognized command errors for abeclean and abematch. The pipeline cannot be reproduced self-contained from the repository.

findings.how_to_check: Modify fs_names1930.dta or touch/truncate a norace*.dta file in divided_file1930_fs_cleaned, then run _matching_master_dofile.do. It will report 'divided_file1930_fs_cleaned complete: reused' without rebuilding.
findings.suggested_fix: Check timestamps or hashes against the underlying inputs (fs_names<yr>.dta and the cleaning script), or introduce a force-rebuild parameter to ensure stale or corrupted intermediate files are not silently reused.
findings.title: FamilySearch divided files are reused solely based on filename presence without checking contents or inputs
findings.what_the_code_does: MATCHING/_matching_master_dofile.do:87-94 compares the list of filenames `built` in `divided_file<y><fstype>` against `want` in `divided_file<y>_ans_cleaned`. If the filename lists match, it assumes the divided directory is complete and skips running 1b_fs_divided_files.do.
findings.why_it_matters: If an earlier run was aborted midway leaving corrupted files, or if fs_names<yr>.dta or the cleaning code in 1b_fs_divided_files.do is altered, subsequent linking runs silently reuse obsolete intermediate files. Link counts may depend on leftover disk artifacts.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied. Review reports and prompt files in review/reports/ were treated as documentation, so claims-vs-code statements against paper draft text could not be verified.

External census datasets on drives D: and F: were not available in this environment, and the Stata pipeline could not be executed; data-dependent counts and live placebo equivalence remain unverified at runtime.
The active ABE implementation on the author's local workstation may differ from repository copies because the current scripts rely on the ambient Stata environment.
structured_output.summary: The new FamilySearch placebo pipeline and verification script (MATCHING/check_placebo.do) are internally coherent and properly check pair uniqueness and attribute equality. However, the pipeline cannot be reproduced on a clean environment because the required ABE commands (abeclean and abematch) are never added to Stata's ado-path. Additionally, intermediate divided-file reuse relies solely on filename listings, risking silent propagation of stale or corrupted data.

verified_clean.evidence: In MATCHING/1b_fs_divided_files.do:49-70, when placebo is 1, fs_namefrst and fs_namelast are set to empty strings. Because fs_frst_used and fs_last_used require non-empty cleaned strings, f_name, l_name, and mi are never overwritten with FamilySearch values.
verified_clean.item: Placebo preprocessing preserves Ancestry names and middle initials without blank substitutions.

verified_clean.evidence: In MATCHING/1b_fs_divided_files.do:46-59, the input data is checked with `isid id`, the merge with fs_names<yr>.dta is 1:1 with keep(1 3), `assert _N==n0` enforces that the record count is unchanged, and `drop _merge` cleans up the merge variable.
verified_clean.item: The FamilySearch name merge preserves the Ancestry universe and enforces key uniqueness.

verified_clean.evidence: In MATCHING/3_append_and_clean_all_links_christian_torbenV2.do:105-121, both side A and side B IDs are merged back to their birthplace divided files with keep(1 3) followed immediately by `assert _merge==3`, guaranteeing every linked ID originated in that birthplace.
verified_clean.item: Linked IDs are strictly required to match the corresponding divided files during link appending.

verified_clean.evidence: The fstype parameter (_fs_cleaned or _fsplacebo_cleaned) is passed consistently through MATCHING/_matching_master_dofile.do:17-19,97-98, MATCHING/2_ABE_matchingV3_master_christian_torben.do:40-49, and MATCHING/3_append_and_clean_all_links_christian_torbenV2.do:67-74,128.
verified_clean.item: Parameter propagation and directory naming for FamilySearch and placebo runs are consistent across all stages.

verified_clean.evidence: In MATCHING/check_placebo.do:16-46, both input datasets require unique `id_A id_B`, a full 1:1 merge verifies _merge!=3 is 0, and each of the seven comparison variables (fiveyr_band, f_name_A, l_name_A, f_name_B, l_name_B, mi1930, mi1940) is explicitly checked for equality.
verified_clean.item: The placebo equality check validates complete pair universe coverage and checks all link attributes.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
